title: guardrails.manifest/1
description: guardrails.manifest.json: the inventory of every guardrail Heimdall enforces, each in exactly one tier. `core` = security and correctness gates: fail-closed, never switchable by any hmd command or config file. `recommended` = cost and discipline guards: on by default, listed, individually switchable by the operator. ANYTHING NOT POSITIVELY CLASSIFIED IS CORE: a row without a tier is invalid, never defaulted. A row describes one guardrail: either a hook of hooks/hooks.json (layer `hook`; `id` and `hook` are the hook's id in hooks/hooks.metadata.json) or a guard that lives inside a hook, a native git hook or a script (any other layer; `hook` names the container, or is null). The file is descriptive: it records the decision, enforcement lives in the guards themselves. THIS FILE IS THE CONTRACT: bin/lib/guardrails_manifest.py enforces it and test/guardrails-manifest-schema.test.sh fails when the two disagree. JSON Schema cannot express cross-field rules, so `x-invariants` lists the ones the validator adds; each is implemented in bin/lib/guardrails_manifest.py. `layer` is free-form kebab-case apart from the reserved value `hook` (conventional values: hook, precheck-bash, precheck-agent, native-git-hook, script). `fails` records the failure mode and is informational only: no rule reads it. `proof` names the suite that proves the guard; that the file exists is checked against the repository by the drift test, not by this schema.

x-invariants.rule: schema is the integer 1: not true, not 1.0, not "1"
ids are unique: one id has one row, so every reader sees the same tier for it
a row with kind guard has a proof: a non-blank string naming the suite that proves it
tier is always stated, never defaulted: anything not positively classified is core, so a row without a tier is invalid

hooks cross-check (validate --hooks-metadata): a row with layer hook is that hook itself (hook equals id, id is a hooks.metadata.json id), and a hook the metadata does not positively mark locked false is locked, so its row has tier core

hooks cross-check: every hooks.metadata.json hook has exactly one row with layer hook; a row with any other layer is a guard inside a hook, names it in hook, and may be recommended even when that hook is locked
no JSON object repeats a key: readers disagree on which value wins, so the file is refused

kind.description: guard = a guardrail; feature = a hook that is not a guardrail, listed so every hook has a row

tier.description: core = never switchable; recommended = on by default, switchable by the operator

layer.description: where it is enforced; `hook` is reserved for a row that IS a hook of hooks/hooks.json

hook.description: the hooks.metadata.json id: the row's own id for layer hook, otherwise the hook the guard lives inside

operator_env.description: the per-process operator override the guard already honours, NAME or NAME=value

proof.description: the suite that proves the guard; required for kind guard

provisional.description: the tier is a placeholder pending an operator decision

guardrails.why: the commit and push gate stack
never pay CI minutes to re-roll a flaky result
